newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices up $0.50-$1.00 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices up $0.50-$1.00 - dealers.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Friday rose $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt as packers competed for live supplies amid light marketings, livestock dealers said.
Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs traded at $56.50 in the country and $57.50 to $58.00 at plants early, sources there said.
Illinois prices climbed $0.50, with country buying stations reporting $56.00 to $57.00 and plants paying up to $58.00, dealers there said.
Indiana and Ohio hog prices were up $0.50 at $55.50 in the country and $56.50 to $57.00 at plants.

Gains were furthered by strong demand early Friday from packers looking to gather a live inventory for Saturday slaughter, dealers said. Improved packer operating margins as a result of brisk pork movement and higher carcass values were generating interest for Saturday operations, they said.
Saturday's slaughter was estimated at market analysts at 60,000 to 100,000 head, compared with 58,000 a week ago and 100,000 a year ago.
Estimated gross cut-out values Thursday were quoted up $1.82 to $1.91 per cwt, with 50.0 loads of fabricated pork and 27.5 loads of trimmings reported sold, USDA said.
